### 任务：分清\"输入\"和\"输出\"（约 10 分钟）\n\n一台自动设:
### Task: Distinguish Between "Inputs" and "Outputs" (About 10 min)

An automated machine has three parts: **sensors and buttons** tell the PLC "what is happening in the field"; these are **inputs (I)**. The **PLC** processes the signals according to its program, then controls **motors, lights, and solenoid valves** to operate; these are **outputs (Q)**.

Lab equipment for this lesson: one conveyor motor M1, one START button, one STOP button, and one LAMP_RUN indicator lamp.

1. Open the control panel and press "Start". Check whether the motor turns and the indicator lamp lights, then press "Stop".
2. Open the PLC panel. Press the buttons and watch the signal values in the I/O monitor table. The I/O table has two sections: "Inputs %I" above and "Outputs %Q" below.
3. Answer the 5 questions below.

**Viewing signals**: PLC1 is already programmed and running, so you don't need to write any code. After entering the lesson, the **Control Panel** window opens automatically. If it is closed, select the lab equipment and click "Control Panel" under "Properties" on the right. Click "**PLC**" (the chip icon) in the vertical toolbar at the far left of the workbench. The **I/O monitor table** is in the lower part of the left panel. It shows each signal's address, name, and current value. TRUE means 1 (signal present); FALSE means 0 (no signal). **Press and hold** a button on the control panel to see the value change (Shift + click locks the button in the pressed state). The "Run Log" below the control panel records each change, for example, `START 0→1`. The 1 / 0 buttons at the end of each I/O table row are for "forcing" signals; you don't need them for this lesson. If you click one, click × to cancel the force.

**Success criteria**: Answer all 5 questions correctly to earn 100 points.

#### Why Learn This

Before learning PLC programming, you must distinguish between inputs and outputs: a PLC can only **read** inputs and **write** outputs.
If you try to "write" to an input or wait for an output to change on its own, your program won't work.
按钮是人\"告诉\" PLC 的，所以是输入。: A button "tells" the PLC something, so it's an input.
接触器、灯是 PLC \"让它动\"的，所以是输出。: The PLC "operates" contactors and lights, so they are outputs.
M1_RUNNING 不是按钮，是电机转起来以后回给 PLC 的信号。: M1_RUNNING isn't a button. It's a signal sent back to the PLC after the motor starts running.
下面哪一个是输入信号: Which of the following is an input signal?
启动按钮是人\"告诉\" PLC 的，PLC 只能读它，所以是输入。M1_RUN: The start button "tells" the PLC something, and the PLC can only read it, so it's an input. M1_RUN and LAMP_RUN are controlled by the PLC, so they are outputs.
输入：PLC 从它读信号: Input: the PLC reads signals from it
输出：PLC 写它，让接触器吸合、电机转: Output: the PLC writes to it to energize the contactor and start the motor
M1_RUN 是 PLC 写的：PLC 让它变 1，接触器吸合，电机才转，所以是: The PLC writes to M1_RUN: the PLC sets it to 1, energizing the contactor, and only then does the motor start. So it is an output (its address starts with %Q).

START 是常开按钮：没按时触点断开是 0，按住时触点接通，读到 1。: START is a normally open button: when it is not pressed, the contact is open and its value is 0. While it is held down, the contact closes and the value read is 1.
电机转起来以后 M1_RUNNING 变成 1，它是: After the motor starts, M1_RUNNING changes to 1. It is
PLC 发给电机的命令: A command from the PLC to the motor
电机回给 PLC 的\"我在转\"，是输入: The motor's "I'm running" signal to the PLC; it is an input

### 任务：弄明白为什么\"没按停止，STOP 却是 1\"（约 15 分钟）:
### Task: Find out why "STOP is 1 when the button isn't pressed" (about 15 minutes)

A button has a pair of contacts, which come in two types:

| Button | When not pressed | When pressed | Common uses |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Normally open (NO)** | Contacts open, signal **0** | Contacts close, signal **1** | Start button |
| **Normally closed (NC)** | Contacts close, signal **1** | Contacts open, signal **0** | Stop button, E-Stop |

On this lesson's conveyor: START is normally open; **STOP and ESTOP (E-Stop) are normally closed**.

1. Don't press anything yet. Open the PLC panel's I/O monitor table and check the values of START, STOP, and ESTOP.
2. Press and hold Stop and watch how STOP changes. Tap E-Stop and watch ESTOP and the conveyor (once pressed, E-Stop remains latched until you press it again to reset).
3. After resetting E-Stop, will the conveyor start moving on its own? Try it.
4. Answer the 6 questions below.

**The most common mistake**: In a ladder diagram, "normally open / normally closed contact" describes **how the signal is used in the program**, not the type of button:
- A normally open contact conducts when the signal is 1; a normally closed contact conducts when the signal is 0.
- STOP is 1 when it isn't pressed, so use a **normally open contact** in the program: not pressed → conducts, motor can run; pressed → changes to 0 → opens, motor stops.
- If you see "the Stop button is normally closed" and draw a normally closed contact, the unpressed signal of 1 opens the contact, so **the motor won't start no matter how you press Start**. Many people get stuck on this in their first PLC lesson.

**How to view signals**: The program is already installed and running on PLC1, so you don't need to write any code. The **Control Panel** window opens automatically when you enter the lesson (if it was closed: select the lab unit, then click **Control Panel** in the **Properties** panel on the right). Click **PLC** (the chip icon) among the vertical icons on the far left of the Workbench. The **I/O monitor table** is in the lower part of the left panel: it shows each signal's address, name, and current value. TRUE means 1 (signal present); FALSE means 0 (no signal). **Press and hold** a button on the Control Panel to see the value change (Shift + click locks it in the pressed state). The **Run Log** below the Control Panel records each change, for example, `START 0→1`. The small 1 / 0 buttons at the end of each I/O table row are for forcing values; you don't need them in this lesson. If you click one, remember to click × to cancel.

#### Why this matters

Stop and E-Stop buttons use normally closed contacts because **if a wire breaks or a connector comes loose, the signal also changes to 0**. The PLC responds as if someone pressed Stop, and the equipment stops.
With a normally open button, a broken wire would make the Stop button ineffective, so the equipment couldn't be stopped in an emergency. This is called "fail-safe design."
常闭按钮没按时触点是接通的，所以读到 1。: When a normally closed button isn't pressed, its contacts are closed, so the signal reads 1.
想一想：线断了，触点就再也接不通了，信号是 0 还是 1？: Think about it: if a wire breaks, the contacts can no longer close. Is the signal 0 or 1?
梯形图的常开触点：\"这个信号是 1，这一格就通\"。STOP 平时是 1，用常: A normally open contact in a ladder diagram means: "When this signal is 1, this contact conducts." STOP is normally 1, so a normally open contact conducts under normal conditions.
没按停止按钮时，STOP 的值是: When the Stop button isn't pressed, the value of STOP is
STOP 是常闭按钮，没按时里面的触点是接通的，所以读到 1。: STOP is a normally closed button. When it isn't pressed, its contact is closed, so the input reads 1.
按住停止按钮时，STOP 的值是: While the Stop button is held down, the value of STOP is
按下常闭按钮，触点被顶开，断开了，所以 STOP 变成 0。: Pressing the normally closed button opens the contact, so STOP changes to 0.
急停拍下以后，ESTOP 的值是: After the E-Stop is pressed, the value of ESTOP is
急停也是常闭的，拍下以后触点断开，ESTOP 变成 0，而且会一直保持，复位以后: The E-Stop is also normally closed. Pressing it opens the contact, so ESTOP changes to 0 and stays there until it is reset, then it returns to 1.
停止按钮的线断了，PLC 读到的 STOP 是: The wire to the Stop button is broken. The PLC reads STOP as
1，和平时一样，没人发现: 1, just like usual. No one notices.
0，和按下停止一样，设备停下来: 0, the same as pressing Stop. The equipment stops.
线断了，触点就再也接不通，PLC 读到的是 0，和有人按了停止一样，设备会停下来: When the wire breaks, the contact can no longer close. The PLC reads 0, just as if someone had pressed Stop, and the equipment stops. This is why Stop buttons use normally closed contacts: faults tend to put the system in a safe state.
梯形图里 STOP 应该画成哪种触点（要求：没按时电机能转，按下停止电机停）: Which contact should STOP use in the ladder diagram? (Requirement: The motor runs when the button isn't pressed and stops when Stop is pressed.)
常开触点（STOP = 1 时导通，按下变 0 就断开）: Normally open contact (conducts when STOP = 1; pressing the button changes it to 0 and opens the contact)
常闭触点（因为停止按钮是常闭的）: Normally closed contact (because the Stop button is normally closed)
梯形图的常开触点是\"信号为 1 时导通\"。STOP 平时是 1，用常开触点平: An NO contact in a ladder diagram conducts when its signal is 1. STOP is normally 1, so an NO contact normally conducts and allows the motor to run. Pressing Stop changes the signal to 0, opening the contact. If you use an NC contact instead, it will normally be open, and pressing Start will not run the motor.
急停复位以后，输送带会不会自己转起来: Will the conveyor restart automatically after the E-Stop is reset?
会，复位就接着转: Yes, it resumes running as soon as the E-Stop is reset.
不会，要再按一次启动: No, you must press Start again.
急停复位只是让 ESTOP 回到 1，程序里的\"运行\"自锁已经断开了，要再按: Resetting the E-Stop only returns ESTOP to 1. The program's "Run" seal-in circuit has already been broken, so you must press Start again to run the conveyor. This prevents the equipment from moving unexpectedly when the E-Stop is reset.
### 任务：看三种传感器各认什么零件（约 15 分钟）\n\n这条分拣线上金属:
### Task: Find out which parts each of three sensors detects (about 15 min)

Metal and plastic parts travel together on this sorting line (about one part every 6 s). Three sensors are installed beside the conveyor:

| Signal | Sensor | How it works |
|---|---|---|
| `IND1` | **Inductive proximity sensor** | Uses a magnetic field; switches to 1 only when **metal** comes within a few millimeters |
| `CAP1` | **Capacitive proximity sensor** | Detects changes in capacitance; can detect metal, plastic, and wood |
| `S1` | **Diffuse-reflective photoelectric sensor** | Emits a light beam; switches to 1 when an object in front reflects the light back |

The PLC program works as follows: When IND1 detects metal, it waits for the part to reach the pusher (S1 switches to 1), then pushes the part into the metal bin. Plastic parts continue to the end of the line.

1. Press "Start" to run the conveyor.
2. Open the I/O Monitor in the PLC panel and watch the IND1, CAP1, and S1 rows. Each value briefly switches to 1 when a part is detected. (If this is too fast, set the speed to 0.5× at the top of the Workbench.)
3. Check the 3D view to identify the passing parts: **gray parts are metal; blue and white parts are plastic**. Answer the questions below.

**How to view signals**: PLC1 already has a program loaded and running. You do not need to write any code. The **Operator Panel** window opens automatically when you enter the lesson (if you close it, select the lab unit and click "Operator Panel" under "Properties" on the right). Click "**PLC**" (the chip icon) in the vertical toolbar at the far left of the Workbench. The **I/O Monitor** is in the lower half of the left pane. It shows each signal's address, name, and current value: TRUE means 1 (signal on), and FALSE means 0 (signal off). **Press and hold** a button on the Operator Panel to see the value change (Shift + click latches the button in the pressed state). The "Run Log" below the Operator Panel records every change, such as `START 0→1`. The small 1 / 0 buttons at the end of each I/O row are for forcing values. You do not need them in this lesson. If you click one, click × to cancel the force.

#### Why learn this?

Sensors are the PLC's "eyes". If you choose the wrong sensor, even a correct program cannot distinguish the parts. For example, if you install a capacitive sensor to identify metal parts, plastic parts will also be treated as metal and pushed aside.
Knowing what each sensor can detect helps you choose the right signal when writing sorting, counting, and positioning programs.
电感式只认金属，电容式什么都认。: Inductive sensors detect only metal; capacitive sensors detect all these materials.
光电开关看的是\"有没有东西挡住/反光\"，不管材料。: Photoelectric sensors detect whether an object blocks or reflects light, regardless of its material.
判断\"是不是金属\"，要用只对金属有反应的那个信号。: To determine whether a part is metal, use the signal that responds only to metal.
金属件经过时，IND1 和 CAP1 分别是: When a metal part passes, what are the values of IND1 and CAP1, respectively?
电感式接近开关 IND1 只认金属，电容式 CAP1 金属塑料都认，所以金属件经: The inductive proximity switch IND1 detects only metal, while the capacitive switch CAP1 detects both metal and plastic. So when a metal part passes by, both are 1.
塑料件经过时，IND1 和 CAP1 分别是: When a plastic part passes by, the states of IND1 and CAP1 are
塑料件不导磁，电感式 IND1 没反应还是 0；电容式 CAP1 什么材料都能感: Plastic is not magnetic, so the inductive switch IND1 does not respond and stays at 0. The capacitive switch CAP1 can detect any material, so it changes to 1.
推杆前的光电开关 S1 对哪种零件有反应: Which types of parts trigger photo-eye S1 in front of the pusher?
光电开关看的是\"前面有没有东西把光反射回来\"，不管是金属还是塑料，零件挡在前: A photo-eye detects whether something in front of it reflects light back. It does not matter whether the part is metal or plastic; when a part blocks the light, the output changes to 1.
PLC 靠哪个信号判断\"这是金属件\": Which signal does the PLC use to determine "this is a metal part"?
三个传感器里只有电感式接近开关 IND1 只对金属有反应，判断\"是不是金属\": Of the three sensors, only the inductive proximity switch IND1 reacts to metal. Use it to determine whether something is metal.
接近开关和光电开关比，最大的不同是: What is the biggest difference between a proximity switch and a photoelectric switch?
接近开关要离得很近（几毫米）才感应得到: A proximity switch only detects objects when they are very close (a few millimeters away).
接近开关能隔着墙感应: A proximity switch can detect objects through a wall.
接近开关只能认塑料: A proximity switch can only detect plastic.
接近开关的感应距离只有几毫米，零件要贴得很近才认得出；光电开关隔得远一些也能看到: A proximity switch has a detection range of only a few millimeters, so the part must be very close to be detected. A photoelectric switch can detect objects from farther away.

### Task: Observe how the actuators move and signal that they are in position (about 15 min)

**Actuators** are the PLC's "hands": the PLC sets an output, and the actuator moves. This color-sorting line has two actuators:

| Actuator | Output signal | Action | Feedback (input) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conveyor motor C1 | `C1_FWD` | 1 = forward, 0 = stopped | — |

Also, when vision sensor V1 detects a part, `V1_DETECT` = 1 and `V1_CODE` gives its color: **1 = blue, 2 = green**. When no part is present, the value is 0. The program pushes green parts into the bin and lets blue parts pass.

### 任务：边看 I/O 边写出工位的动作顺序（约 20 分钟）\n\n这是一:
### Task: Observe the I/O and write down the workstation's action sequence (about 20 minutes)

This is a machining workstation: hopper E1 periodically releases parts onto the conveyor. A part reaches the workstation and is stopped by **stopper ST1**, is "machined" for a while, then the stopper lowers to release it, and the part travels to the end of the line.

| Signal | Direction | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `E1_RELEASE` | Output | Hopper release: changes from 0 to 1 to release one part |
| `C1_FWD` | Output | Conveyor forward |
| `ST1_RAISE` | Output | 1 = stopper raised to hold the part, 0 = lowered to release it |
| `S1` | Input | Workstation position photo-eye: 1 when a part reaches the stopper |
| `LAMP_WORK` | Output | Machining indicator lamp |
| `START` / `STOP` / `ESTOP` | Input | Start (normally open) / Stop (normally closed) / E-Stop (normally closed) |

1. Press "Start." Watch the S1, LAMP_WORK, and ST1_RAISE rows in the I/O monitor table on the PLC panel. See how they change as a part arrives at and leaves the workstation.
2. Count how often the hopper releases a part and how long the machining lamp stays on. (The simulation clock at the top of the Workbench can serve as a stopwatch.)
3. While the simulation is running, press "Stop" once and see which outputs change to 0.
4. Answer the 6 questions below.

**How to view signals**: PLC1 already has a program loaded and running; you do not need to write one. The **Control Panel** window opens automatically when you enter the lesson. If it is closed, select the lab unit, then click "Control Panel" in the "Properties" panel on the right. Click "**PLC**" (the chip icon) in the vertical toolbar on the far left of the Workbench. The **I/O monitor table** is in the lower part of the left panel: it shows each signal's address, name, and current value. TRUE means 1 (signal on); FALSE means 0 (signal off). **Press and hold** a button on the Control Panel to see the value change. (Shift + click locks the button in the pressed position.) The "Run Log" below the Control Panel records each change, for example, `START 0→1`. The 1 / 0 buttons at the end of each I/O table row are for "forcing" signals. You do not need them in this lesson; if you click one, remember to click × to cancel.

#### Why this matters

A PLC program is essentially a chain of "detect an input → change an output → wait for the next input" steps.
If you can describe a machine's action sequence by reading its I/O table, writing the program is just translating that sequence. When equipment fails, you also check which expected signal did not arrive.

运行中按停止会怎样: What happens if you press Stop while the system is running?
输送带停、料仓不再放料、运行灯灭: The conveyor stops, the hopper stops releasing parts, and the Run light turns off.
只有运行灯灭，输送带接着转: Only the Run light turns off; the conveyor keeps running.
挡停落下，零件全部放行: The stopper lowers, releasing all parts.
按停止以后程序里的\"运行\"标志断开，跟着它的输送带、料仓放料、运行灯一起变: When you press Stop, the program's "Run" flag turns off, so the conveyor, hopper feed, and Run light controlled by it all switch to 0.
